{{politics of India}}

The results of [[India]]'s [[Elections in India|general elections]] to constitute [[18th Lok Sabha]], held in [[2024 Indian general election|April–June 2024]] were announced on 4 and 5 June 2024.<ref name = NDTV5June>{{Cite web |title=Election Results 2024: All Seats Declared, Check Which Party Won How Many |url=https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/2024-lok-sabha-election-results-declared-bjp-wins-in-240-congress-in-99-5820696 |access-date=2024-06-05 |website=NDTV.com}}</ref> The main contenders were two alliance groups of the Incumbent [[National Democratic Alliance (India)|National Democratic Alliance]] (N.D.A) led by [[Bharatiya Janata Party]]; and the Opposition [[Indian National Developmental Inclusive Alliance]] (I.N.D.I.A) led by [[Indian National Congress]].<ref name =CNBC1>{{cite news|url=https://www.cnbc.com/2024/06/04/indias-narendra-modi-declares-victory-despite-election-blow.html|title=India's Narendra Modi declares victory despite election blow|first=Matt|last=Clinch|publisher=CNBC|date=4 June 2024|accessdate=4 June 2024|archive-date=4 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240604213407/https://www.cnbc.com/2024/06/04/indias-narendra-modi-declares-victory-despite-election-blow.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.cnn.com/asia/live-news/india-general-election-results-06-04-24-intl-hnk/index.html|title=India decides: Modi declares victory in election but his party faces shock losses|first1=Rhea|last1=Mogul|first2=Jessie|last2=Yeung|first3=Diksha|last3=Madhok|first4=Antoinette|last4=Radford|publisher=CNN|date=4 June 2024|accessdate=4 June 2024|archive-date=4 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240604051935/https://www.cnn.com/asia/live-news/india-general-election-results-06-04-24-intl-hnk/index.html|url-status=live}}</ref> In the [[18th Lok Sabha|legislative house]] of 543 seats, the incumbent [[National Democratic Alliance|NDA Alliance]] secured majority with 293 seats, which included [[Bharatiya Janata Party|BJP]] party's 240 seats,<ref name=TH5June>{{Cite web |last=Sinha |first=Shishir |date=5 June 2024 |title=NDA elects Modi as leader, President dissolves Lok Sabha |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/news/elections/nda-elects-modi-as-leader-president-dissolves-lok-sabha/article68255830.ece |access-date=5 June 2024 |website=BusinessLine |language=en |archive-date=5 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240605153429/https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/news/elections/nda-elects-modi-as-leader-president-dissolves-lok-sabha/article68255830.ece |url-status=live }}</ref> while the opposition [[Indian National Developmental Inclusive Alliance|INDIA Alliance]]  got 234 seats, including the [[Indian National Congress|Congress]] party's 99 seats.<ref name=BS5June>{{Cite news |last=Aggarwal |first=Raghav |date=4 June 2024 |title=INDIA alliance bloc's combined strength plays spoilsport for BJP in 2 biggest states |url=https://www.business-standard.com/elections/lok-sabha-election/india-bloc-s-combined-strength-plays-spoilsport-for-bjp-in-2-biggest-states-124060401570_1.html |access-date=5 June 2024 |work=Business Standard |archive-date=4 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240604151957/https://www.business-standard.com/elections/lok-sabha-election/india-bloc-s-combined-strength-plays-spoilsport-for-bjp-in-2-biggest-states-124060401570_1.html |url-status=live }}</ref> On June 9, 2024, [[Narendra Modi]] took oath as Prime Minister, having been elected the leader of the NDA alliance, though BJP lost its majority.<ref name=BBC9June>{{Cite news |date=9 June 2024 |title=Narendra Modi sworn in for third term at grand ceremony in Delhi |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c3ggnm7r75yo |access-date=10 June 2024 |work=BBC |archive-date=9 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240609141931/https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c3ggnm7r75yo |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Overview ==

The BJP-led NDA surpassed the majority threshold of 272 and won 293 seats. However, unlike the [[2019 Indian general election|previous election]], the BJP did not win a majority in both houses of parliament having only won 240 seats (losing 63 seats from the 303 seats they previously held since 2019 as well as losing their 10-year long benefit of being the sole-controller of both houses of parliament since 2014) in the [[Lok Sabha]].<ref name = NDTV5June>{{Cite web |title=Election Results 2024: All Seats Declared, Check Which Party Won How Many |url=https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/2024-lok-sabha-election-results-declared-bjp-wins-in-240-congress-in-99-5820696 |access-date=2024-06-05 |website=NDTV.com}}</ref> However, [[Narendra Modi]] became the second Indian prime minister to be re-elected for a third consecutive term, since [[Jawaharlal Nehru]]'s re-election in [[1962 Indian general election|1962]], the third Indian prime minister to be able to rule for more than 10 years after Nehru (15 years) & [[Indira Gandhi]] (14 years) & the second BJP leader after [[Atal Bihari Vajpayee]] to be able to lead the party into becoming the single largest party in the Lok Sabha thrice.

The INC-led INDIA alliance gained 234 seats out of which 99 were won by the Congress Party. 37 seats were won by the [[Samajwadi Party|SP]] while 29 seats from [[West Bengal]] were won by the [[Mamata Banerjee]]-led [[Trinamool Congress]]. The final wins by the alliance were stronger than previous predictions from exit polls.<ref name=BBC9June>{{Cite news |date=9 June 2024 |title=Narendra Modi sworn in for third term at grand ceremony in Delhi |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c3ggnm7r75yo |access-date=10 June 2024 |work=BBC |archive-date=9 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240609141931/https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c3ggnm7r75yo |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=BS5June/>

The BJP lost 63 seats while its two main partners, the [[Telugu Desam Party|TDP]] and the [[Janata Dal (United)|JD(U)]], gained 13 seats and lost 4, respectively. Within the opposition alliance, the Congress party gained 47 seats, the SP gained 32 seats, and the Trinamool Congress gained 7 
seats. [[Uttar Pradesh]], West Bengal and [[Maharashtra]] had earlier indications of an overwhelming BJP and allies victory but ultimately were won by the opposition with the SP winning in UP, the Trinamool Congress in Bengal and the [[Shiv Sena (UBT)|SS-UBT]], the Congress Party and the [[Nationalist Congress Party – Sharadchandra Pawar|NCP-SP]] winning Maharashtra.<ref name=BS5June/>

According to [[Reuters]], a key reason for BJP losing its majority in 2024 was the narrative by the Opposition parties that BJP's target of [[Abki Baar 400 Paar|obtaining more than 400 seats]] was aimed to bring about sweeping amendments to the Constitution involving removal of [[Gandhism|Gandhian ideals]] as [[Directive Principles|the guiding principles of the government]] & replacing them with its [[Hindutva]] narrative, the most notable among the proposed changes being altering the [[Reservation in India|reservation quotas]], based on the remarks by some prominent BJP leaders.<ref name=Reuters14June>{{Cite news |date=14 June 2024 |title=India's opposition leveraged caste and constitution to shock Modi in election |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/india/indias-opposition-leveraged-caste-constitution-shock-modi-election-2024-06-14/ |access-date=15 June 2024 |work=Reuters}}</ref>

According to the national data from the [[Centre for the Study of Developing Societies]] (CSDS) – Lokniti National Election Studies published in ''[[The Hindu]]'', the [[National Democratic Alliance (India)|National Democratic Alliance]] (NDA) maintained a 3 percentage point lead in the overall national vote share (43% to 40%) over the [[INDIA (alliance)|INDIA alliance]].<ref name="CSDSLokniti2024Overall">{{cite news |author=Lokniti-CSDS |date=6 June 2024 |title=Lok Sabha elections 2024 {{!}} CSDS-Lokniti post-poll survey |url=https://thehindu.com |work=[[The Hindu]] |access-date=15 June 2024}}</ref> The NDA maintained its strongest age advantage among young voters aged 18–25, capturing 46% of their vote compared to 33% for the INDIA bloc,<ref name="CSDSYouth2024">{{cite news |author=Kumar, Sanjay|author2=Bandhu, Fuhaar |date=7 June 2024 |title=CSDS-Lokniti post-poll survey: BJP maintains advantage among young voters |url=https://thehindu.com |work=[[The Hindu]] |access-date=21 June 2024}}</ref> The INDIA alliance performed best among non-literate voters, leading the NDA by 42% to 38%,<ref name="CSDSLokniti2024Overall" /> whereas the NDA's support scaled up with higher education and economic affluence, peaking at 45% among graduates and 46% among the wealthiest class.<ref name="CSDSLokniti2024Overall" /><ref name="CSDSEcon2024">{{cite news |last=Borbora |first=A. P. |date=7 June 2024 |title=CSDS-Lokniti post-poll survey: The BJP's pro-rich skew becomes moderate |url=https://thehindu.com |work=[[The Hindu]] |access-date=15 June 2024}}</ref> Geographically, the spatial divide showed the NDA dominating large metropolitan cities and urban zones with a 45% vote share,<ref name="CSDSLocality2024">{{cite news |author=Lokniti-CSDS |date=7 June 2024 |title=CSDS-Lokniti post-poll survey: How urban and rural India voted |url=https://thehindu.com |work=[[The Hindu]] |access-date=15 June 2024}}</ref> but while the NDA bloc surged into a lead in small, semi-urban towns (42% to 41%), rural villages remained highly competitive with the NDA retaining a narrow 42% to 41% edge overall.<ref name="CSDSLocality2024" /> In terms of communities, the NDA maintained a massive upper-caste Hindu anchor (61%) and held comfortable margins among Other Backward Classes (OBCs), while Scheduled Castes (Dalits) tied perfectly at 31% for both coalitions.<ref name="CSDSLokniti2024Overall" /> Religious minorities, especially the Muslims heavily consolidated behind the opposition, with 65% of Muslims voting for the INDIA alliance,<ref name="CSDSMinorities2024">{{cite news |last=Menon |first=Aditya |date=7 June 2024 |title=NDA's Biggest Gains & Losses Were Among 2 Minority Groups |url=https://thequint.com |work=[[The Quint]] |access-date=21 June 2024}}</ref>
